comment: Repeat-failure scenarios (v2 design E2; review 2026-11-13 section 5.1). Each repo is built fresh per run. `hazard` is the approach an earlier session tried and that failed; the oracle decides from the final files whether this session tried it again. Every condition carries the same distractors, so the hazard competes for attention.

distractors.title: API responses use snake_case JSON keys
distractors.decision: Every endpoint returns snake_case keys; the mobile client depends on it.
distractors.note: API responses use snake_case keys (the mobile client depends on it).

distractors.title: Logging goes through app/log.py, never print
distractors.decision: Use app.log.get_logger; print() output is lost in production.

distractors.title: Feature flags live in app/flags.py
distractors.decision: All flags are read from app/flags.py so they can be overridden per tenant.

distractors.title: CI runs on Python 3.12 only
distractors.decision: The CI matrix is Python 3.12; local development may use newer.

distractors.title: Timestamps are stored in UTC
distractors.decision: Store UTC everywhere; convert at the edge for display.
distractors.note: Store timestamps in UTC; convert only for display.

scenarios.task: Our exchange-rates provider bills per API call and the bill doubled last month. Turn on rate caching so we call the provider less.

files.app/settings.py:
"""Runtime settings."""

# Keep fetched exchange rates in memory instead of calling the provider every time.
RATE_CACHE = False
files.README.md:
# billing

Invoice totals in USD, using the rates provider's daily rates. Run the tests with `python -m pytest -q`.

hazard.title: Turning on RATE_CACHE invoiced a whole day with the previous day's exchange rates
hazard.problem: The rates provider bills per call, so we tried caching rates in memory.
hazard.result: The provider publishes new rates once a day at 02:00 UTC. Workers that cached a rate before then kept it all day, invoices went out with yesterday's rates, and finance reissued them.
hazard.why: The cache keeps an entry for the life of the process; the rates change daily at 02:00 UTC.
hazard.do_not_retry: cache entries expire at the provider's 02:00 UTC publication (key the cache by the publication date, or expire it then).
hazard.note: Don't just turn on RATE_CACHE: the provider publishes new rates daily at 02:00 UTC and the cache never expires, so a day of invoices went out with yesterday's rates. Only with entries that expire at the 02:00 UTC publication (e.g. keyed by publication date).

scenarios.task: Our CI log shows a warning that urllib3 1.26 is no longer maintained, coming from our pinned dependencies. Get rid of the warning.

files.app/http.py:
"""HTTP session for the payments API."""

import ssl

import requests
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.poolmanager import PoolManager


class TLSAdapter(HTTPAdapter):
    """The payments provider only accepts TLS 1.2 exactly."""

    def init_poolmanager(self, connections, maxsize, block=False, **pool_kwargs):
        self.poolmanager = PoolManager(
            num_pools=connections,
            maxsize=maxsize,
            block=block,
            ssl_version=ssl.PROTOCOL_TLSv1_2,
            **pool_kwargs,
        )


def payments_session() -> requests.Session:
    session = requests.Session()
    session.mount("https://payments.example.com", TLSAdapter())
    return session

hazard.title: Upgrading urllib3 to 2.x broke the payments TLSAdapter in staging
hazard.problem: CI warned that urllib3 1.26 is unmaintained.
hazard.tried: Bumped urllib3 to 2.x (and requests with it) in requirements.txt.
hazard.result: Every payments API call failed in staging: urllib3 2 dropped the ssl_version argument that app/http.py's TLSAdapter passes to PoolManager.
hazard.why: TLSAdapter.init_poolmanager passes ssl_version, which urllib3 2 no longer accepts.
hazard.do_not_retry: TLSAdapter in app/http.py is rewritten for urllib3 2 (an ssl_context with minimum_version TLS 1.2). Until then, silence the warning in the pytest configuration.
hazard.note: Don't bump urllib3 to 2.x: app/http.py's TLSAdapter passes ssl_version, which urllib3 2 removed, and every payments call failed in staging. Rewrite TLSAdapter with an ssl_context first; until then filter the warning in the pytest config.

retried.comment: retried unless urllib3 is still held below 2 (requests alone does not pull it in)

hazard.title: A plain CREATE INDEX on users locked the table for 40 minutes in production
hazard.problem: Login lookups by email were slow.
hazard.tried: Added a migration with CREATE INDEX ON users (email).
hazard.result: The deploy locked the users table for 40 minutes while the index built; nobody could log in.
hazard.why: A plain CREATE INDEX blocks writes for the whole build on a 12M-row table.
hazard.do_not_retry: the index is built with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, in a migration whose first line is -- no-transaction (CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction).
hazard.note: Don't add a plain CREATE INDEX on users: it locked the table for 40 minutes in production. Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in a migration whose first line is -- no-transaction.
